16a

The frequency of red light is lower than the frequency of blue light, so based on the equation photons in the blue light beam carry more energy than the photons in the red light beam.

The experiment shows that when the energy of the photons in the light beam is increased, one photoelectron is emitted per incident photon, which is evidence for the particle nature of light. 

The energy of an electromagnetic wave is independent of the frequency of the wave, so based on the wave theory of light, no change should occur when blue light is used instead of red light.

OR

Based on the wave theory for light, electrons would not be emitted instantaneously, because energy would have to be built up in order for electron emission to happen.

In an experiment to demonstrate the photoelectric effect, a student first uses red monochromatic light and then blue monochromatic light. The student observes that when she shines red light on a metal surface, no electrons are emitted from the surface; however when she shines blue light on the same metal surface, photoelectrons are emitted instantaneously. 

a. Explain how these observations provide evidence for the particle nature of light, but not for the wave nature of light.
